## Short answer

- **Rendering:** `ramify/presentation/project-view` — a new bare-SVG component beside `ModuleGraphRadial`, reusing the scope/roll-up functions that already decide what the diagram shows.
- **Command:** `ramify/cli` — a new verb next to `materializeCommand`.
- **They cannot touch each other.** `cli` is `[dispatch]`-only and the renderer is `ui`-tagged, so a third, `[dispatch, ui]`-carrying owner has to do the emitting (React element → string → file). Details below.

## Why project-view renders it

`ramify/presentation/project-view` already owns the behavioral dependency diagram end to end:

- Its purpose is exactly this picture — "a pure browser-facing behavioral dependency diagram with a detail panel" (`.ramify-architect/presentation/project-view/module.json:12`).
- It owns the diagram's **data contract**: `DependencyGraphModel` (`presentation/project-view/supporting.jsonl:15`) and `ProjectExplorerModel` (`supporting.jsonl:6`), both in `src/interfaces/`.
- It owns **what is drawn**: `dependencyScope`, `scopeDependencyLinks`, `scopeEnd`, `edgeStatus`, `scopeLinkCounts` (`presentation/project-view/behavior.jsonl:15,44,45,16,46`), plus the visual encodings `linkWidth` ("bounded logarithmic width", `behavior.jsonl:34`), `nodeDiameters` (`behavior.jsonl:38`), `ownSourceNodeId` (`behavior.jsonl:8`) and `getPresentationClassColor` (`behavior.jsonl:31`). These are pure and already tested headlessly (`presentation/project-view/tests.jsonl:1`, BD30–BD60 suites at `tests.jsonl:5–7`).

You cannot reuse `ModuleGraphRadial` itself: it is a React Flow component, not an `<svg>`. `buildGraphEdges` returns React Flow `Edge[]` (`behavior.jsonl:9`), `FitTarget` is "the part of a React Flow instance fitting needs" (`supporting.jsonl:44`), `useAutoFit` needs a live instance and resize observations (`behavior.jsonl:48`), and a test asserts it "preserves graph framework state while presentation-class filtering rerenders" (`tests.jsonl:1`). So add a second renderer over the same facts.

That pairing is the established pattern in the parent: `ramify/presentation` ships `ModelDiagram`/`ModelDiagramSvg`, whose doc reads "The bare `<svg>`. This is what the static emitter renders" (`presentation/behavior.jsonl:4`), with the same split for `FocusDiagramSvg` and `TreeDiagramSvg` (`presentation/behavior.jsonl:2,6`) and a `diagramStylesheet` "embedded in the `<svg>`" (`presentation/behavior.jsonl:26`).

Two concrete gaps to plan for:

- **Placement.** `ramify/presentation/layout` exposes `placeTree`, `placeNodes`, `placeChords`, `placeFocus`, `placeLanes`, `placeLegend` (`presentation/layout/behavior.jsonl:1,10,6,7,8,9`) — no radial placement. `placeTree` is already a behavioral dependency of project-view (`presentation/layout/behavior.jsonl:1`), so either reuse it for a static arrangement or add a neutral radial placement to `layout`.
- **Byte stability.** `ramify/presentation/layout#r` rounds "so emitted SVG is byte-identical run to run" (`presentation/layout/behavior.jsonl:20`) but is exposed only to its parent, with no re-exposure to descendants — unlike `placeTree`. `ramify/presentation` must re-expose `r` to its descendants before project-view can use it.

## Why the CLI owns the command

`ramify/cli` owns every verb and the exit code: `runCli` (`cli/behavior.jsonl:1`), `parseArguments`, which "validate[s] the entire invocation before dispatch" (`cli/behavior.jsonl:13`), and one function per command — `checkCommand`, `watchCommand`, `exploreCommand`, `materializeCommand` (`cli/behavior.jsonl:5,17,9,12`), with the usage string at `cli/supporting.jsonl:10`. `materializeCommand` is the precedent: a command that turns one analyzed revision into generated files.

Make it a **new verb**, not `materialize --view svg`. `materialize`'s view IDs are fixed at `'api' | 'architect'` in the root's service vocabulary (`.ramify-architect/supporting.jsonl:3`) and again in the daemon (`daemon/supporting.jsonl:20`), and those views are rendered inside the analysis/daemon path (`ramify/analysis#renderArchitectView`, `analysis/behavior.jsonl:4`; `ramify/daemon#createFilesystemApiViewPublisher`, `.ramify-architect/README.md:43`). The daemon is `[dispatch]` and must stay free of UI dependencies, so it cannot render React. The diagram facts already have their own service operation — `dependencyDiagram` in `ServiceOperation`/`ServiceCapability` (`.ramify-architect/supporting.jsonl:15,16`), produced by `ramify/analysis#analyzeDependencyDiagram` (`analysis/behavior.jsonl:1`) — so the command should request that and render on the client side of the daemon.

## The part that needs a decision: who emits

`ramify/cli` is `[dispatch]` (`.ramify-architect/README.md:38`) and the renderer will be `ui`-tagged. `ui` carries the required-importer rule: "a symbol tagged `ui` may be imported only by source carrying `ui`, for both value and type-only imports" (`docs/model/cross-module-importability.principles.md:292–294`). The root cannot wire it either: `ramify` is `[dispatch]` (`.ramify-architect/module.json:7`), its README says it "keeps executable dispatch separate from portable model and presentation entries" (`module.json:12`), and its `uses` list contains no presentation module (`module.json:18–26`). A lazy import is no escape — lazy-import member selections check their selected originals.

Today exactly one module bridges the two sides: `ramify/explorer`, tagged `[browser, dispatch, ui]` (`explorer/module.json:7`), the only consumer of project-view (`explorer/module.json:19`; `presentation/project-view/module.json:25–27`) and also a consumer of `ramify/service-api` (`explorer/module.json:20`).

My recommendation: **a new root child, e.g. `ramify/report [dispatch, ui]`, invoked as a one-shot child process**, rather than hanging the emitter on `ramify/explorer`.

- The emitter writes a file, so its symbol must not carry `browser`.
